venue.name: McLean Mill National Historic Site
venue.description: McLean Mill National Historic Site is a former steam-powered sawmill and logging operation on 12.8 hectares in the Alberni Valley, with 35 buildings and structures set around a mill pond. The R.B. McLean Lumber Company ran here as a family business from 1926 to 1965, and the site was designated a national historic site of Canada in 1989. It is operated by the Alberni Valley Chamber of Commerce under agreement with the City of Port Alberni. The site is currently closed for the season, so the administration office, heritage buildings, gift shop and washrooms are shut, but the grounds stay open from dawn to dusk and guided tours for groups are still taken by reservation with at least seven days notice.
venue.address: 5633 Smith Road, Port Alberni, BC, V9Y 8M1

facility_notes.washrooms: Except for the R.B. McLean house, that has been rebuilt as a modern facility and contains public washrooms, the other buildings have been partially restored. Access to indoor washrooms (during open hours, no showers). While the site is closed for the season the washrooms are closed.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Back on the main path, stairs lead up to a viewing gallery running along the far side of the mill that allows safe viewing of the various processes even when the mill is operating. There is an elevator for those unable to climb the stairs.

restrictions: Please obey all site signage for your safety.
Bring your furry friends (please keep them on leash on the site as there is a dog on the premises) and please pick up after your pets (that includes horses, too).
Please keep a SLOW respectful speed when passing through the site to ensure the safety of your fellow visitors.
venue.hours_notes: The site is open from dawn to dusk, 365 days a year for you to explore at your own risk. The staffed hours when the Mill Store, heritage buildings and washrooms are open are not published.
venue.seasonal_notes: McLean Mill National Historic Site is now CLOSED for the season. The Historic Site is accessible from dawn to dusk at your own risk. The Administration Office, Historic buildings, Gift Shop and washrooms are closed. Self Guided Tours are not available at this time and the Gift Shop is not available at this time. Guided tours for groups are listed as open for reservations only, and can be accommodated most days with at least 7 days notice. Private tours are booking for the 2026 season. The train (Alberni Pacific Railway) is not running to McLean Mill this year. The site does not publish the dates its staffed season opens or closes.

programs.name: Private or group guided tour
programs.description: A historic interpreter leads the group through the site to cover the history of the mill and camp life. Tours run about an hour and a half and can be tailored to the group. Groups can be accommodated most days with at least seven days notice, arranged by email. The rate is a $50 tour guide fee plus a charge per person, and GST and a Heritage Fee are added to all tours. Private tours are booking for the 2026 season.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the site behind a guide, from the camp life buildings and the blacksmith shop and bunkhouse down across the dam to the mill pond and the steam-driven sawmill, going into the heritage buildings that are set up to explore. Inside the mill, stairs lead up to a viewing gallery that looks down on the saws, with an elevator for anyone who cannot climb them.
programs.our_note: It is about ninety minutes on foot around an outdoor working site, which is long for under-fives, and the tour can be tailored, so say who is coming when you email. The published rates start at age 6, so ask what a group of preschoolers actually pays. Nothing on the site says how many children can come at once or whether there is anywhere indoors to eat.
programs.practical_summary: There are public washrooms in the rebuilt McLean house and an elevator inside the mill, and the visit is otherwise outdoors across a large historic site. Indoor lunch space, rain backup, bus parking and any limit on group size are not stated, so it is worth a call before you book.
programs.extra_fees_note: A $50 tour guide fee applies on top of the per person rates. GST and a Heritage Fee are applicable on all tours. Children under the age of 5 get in free, and youth 13 to 18 and students pay $12.

programs.name: Self-guided tour
programs.description: During the staffed season, admission covers a self-guided walking tour. The site map is picked up at the Mill Store in the Admin Building, and a 24 stop heritage signage program runs through the site. Some of the heritage buildings are set up to go inside. Admission is $10 for adults 18 and over, $5 for students 8 to 17, $5 for seniors 65 and over, and free for children 7 and under. Self-guided tours are not available while the site is closed for the season.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a paper map around the site at their own pace, reading the 24 numbered heritage signs and going into the heritage buildings that are open, from the office and cookhouse to the blacksmith shop and the bunkhouse. The path from the visitor area runs through second growth forest, crosses the dam beside the log pond and reaches the steam sawmill, where stairs lead up to a viewing gallery above the saws.
programs.our_note: No guide comes with you, and the route crosses a dam beside a log pond and goes through a working sawmill, so work out the adult count yourself. Children 7 and under go in free, which makes this the cheaper option for a young group. The site is shut for the season right now, so check it has reopened before you pick a date.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are in the rebuilt McLean house, the map is handed out at the Mill Store, and the visit is mostly outdoors across a large site. The staffed opening hours, indoor lunch space, rain backup and bus parking are not stated anywhere, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Kids 7 and under are free. Seniors 65 and over pay the same $5 as students.
programs.evidence: Admission is $10/adults (18+), $5/students (8-17), $5/seniors (65+), kids 7 and under are free.

programs.name: Grounds access, dawn to dusk
programs.description: The grounds are open from dawn to dusk, 365 days a year, to explore at your own risk, with no admission charge and no staff on site. While the site is closed for the season the administration office, the heritage buildings, the gift shop and the washrooms are all shut. Leashed pets are welcome. The site gives access to a variety of trails for hiking, biking and horseback riding, including the Log Train Trail.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the roads and paths of the mill site in the open air, past the outsides of the heritage buildings and around the log pond, and carry on to the trails that run off the site.
programs.our_note: This is the fallback when the site is closed for the season, and it is genuinely just a walk outdoors with nothing open, no washrooms and nobody on duty. Signs mark what is off limits, and children need an adult close by around the pond and the machinery. There is a dog living on the premises, worth knowing if anyone in the group is nervous of dogs.
programs.practical_summary: Free, outdoors and open every day from dawn to dusk. Nothing else is open while the site is closed for the season, so there are no washrooms, no shelter and no staff, and bus parking is not stated.
programs.evidence: The site is open from dawn to dusk, 365 days a year for you to explore at your own risk.
